description:
Redwood Inference is running a focused “FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint” to quantify and improve the performance of quantization-friendly execution paths in the serving runtime, with an emphasis on kernel behavior and scheduler interactions under realistic hosted traffic shapes.

Goals:
- Produce a defensible benchmark report for FP8 and INT8 across Redwood’s top hosted models and primary GPU SKUs, covering both microbenchmarks (kernel-level) and end-to-end serving metrics.
- Identify and implement a small, high-confidence set of kernel/scheduling changes (or configuration defaults) that improve cost-per-token and p95 latency without regressing correctness/quality.
- Establish repeatable methodology and automation: consistent environments, pinned runtime versions, standardized prompts/workloads, regression thresholds, and dashboards.

Scope:
- Models: top hosted chat/completions models (e.g., Llama-family, Qwen-family, Mistral-family) with representative prompt length distributions (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy) and batch/streaming modes.
- Hardware: major fleet GPUs (e.g., A100, H100/H200, L40S; optionally MI300X where available) across the primary regions used in perf-lab.
- Runtime components: quantized GEMM/attention kernels (FP8/INT8), kernel auto-selection, KV-cache interaction points, scheduler policies that affect prefill/decode interleaving and batching.
- Deliverables: benchmark matrix + methodology docs, harness updates, perf-canary gating/thresholds, and a written sprint report with recommended defaults and follow-up roadmap.

Non-goals:
- Broad product/UX changes, customer-facing pricing or packaging updates.
- Large model-quality research beyond ensuring quantization changes do not violate Redwood’s guardrails.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Isabella Rossi.
- Runtime Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Julian Moore.
- Performance Benchmarks / Harness: Rina Kobayashi, Noah Patel.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Arjun Desai, Priyanka Bose (quant profiles + sanity evals).
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant (dashboards, gating, perf lab reliability).
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien (branching, release notes, canary policy).

Timeline (sprint-style):
- Week 1: finalize benchmark spec + environments; implement harness changes; collect baselines.
- Week 2: run full matrix; investigate anomalies; land targeted optimizations/config changes; add dashboards and gating.
- End of sprint: publish report + ADRs, ship changes behind safe rollout knobs, and schedule follow-ups for remaining gaps.

files.description: Sprint charter: objectives, success metrics, in/out of scope, staffing, and expected artifacts.
Benchmark methodology: environment pinning, clock/power settings, warmup, repetitions, statistical reporting, and how to avoid common perf pitfalls.
Definition of ‘top hosted’ models + workloads: prompt sets, sequence length distributions, concurrency levels, streaming vs non-streaming, and decoding parameters.
GPU coverage plan: instance types, driver/CUDA versions, MIG settings (if any), known hardware quirks, and capacity constraints.
ADR defining primary metrics (TTFT, TPOT, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, cost proxy) and aggregation rules across runs and regions.
ADR: FP8 format choice (e4m3/e5m2), accumulation type, scaling strategy, and correctness tolerances for inference.
Operational runbook for executing the benchmark suite (commands, configs, data upload, troubleshooting failed runs).
Profiling playbook addendum: Nsight/CUPTI guidance, kernel timeline interpretation, and how to attribute latency to prefill vs decode.
Proposed regression thresholds and gating policy for quantized paths; when to block a release vs allow with mitigation.
Final sprint report: baseline results, deltas from landed changes, anomaly explanations, recommended defaults, and follow-up items.
Quantization profile compatibility notes per model family: supported ops, fallback behavior, and known accuracy-sensitive layers.
Dashboard spec for quant perf: panels, tags (model/GPU/runtime version), and alerting thresholds for regressions.

PR: Add runtime config knob to force specific quant kernel family for A/B experiments; docs and safe defaults.
